open_question: Is the per-key fast path just elapsed post-keyup time?
strongest_evidence: Raw CDP ordinary waits from about 4ms through 5008ms stay around 21-24ms keypress p50.
what_is_closed: Ordinary sleeping, queued-JS drain, and browser rest time are not sufficient explanations.
next_probe: No more ordinary-wait extensions unless a different browser build changes the result.

open_question: Is one generic renderer task, timer, or frame checkpoint enough?
strongest_evidence: A single Runtime.evaluate, setTimeout(0), or RAF checkpoint improves only partway and does not reach the trace-on page.evaluate band.
what_is_closed: The missing boundary is narrower than task, timer, or frame progression.
remaining_unknown: Which runtime/protocol side effect accumulates when checkpoints are repeated.
next_probe: Trace direct Runtime.evaluate and Runtime.callFunctionOn repeat grids with Chromium scheduler/runtime categories.

open_question: Do Playwright trace snapshots explain the full per-key fast path?
current_answer: Yes for the default trace-on performance configuration.
strongest_evidence: With trace on, per-key keyboard.press and raw CDP plus page.evaluate are about 11.3ms; with trace off they are about 22.1ms and 17.4ms.
what_is_closed: Trace-on per-key Playwright actions are a measurement perturbation, not a human-typing model.
remaining_unknown: Which snapshot subcommand or renderer state transition causes the speedup.
next_probe: Compare trace-on captureSnapshot windows with trace-off repeated Runtime.callFunctionOn windows in the same Chromium scheduler trace.

open_question: Can direct runtime checkpoints reproduce the trace-off residual?
strongest_evidence: Direct runtime calls move raw CDP from 21.5ms to about 15-16ms at x7 and about 13ms at x17.
what_is_closed: A unique Playwright utility-script or locator semantic action is not required.
remaining_unknown: Whether the driver is V8 microtask state, renderer scheduler priority, input queue state, cache/frequency side effects, or a combination.
next_probe: Hold raw CDP input fixed, vary checkpoint count, and trace renderer scheduler/runtime state around the prior keyup and next keydown.

open_question: Is the checkpoint effect enough to explain Gutenberg-scale movement by itself?
strongest_evidence: Native contenteditable moves only about 0.3-0.4ms while Gutenberg moves by several milliseconds.
what_is_closed: The browser/runtime trigger is real, but Gutenberg's data/RichText fanout supplies the scale.
remaining_unknown: How much of the amplified cost survives realistic user/plugin workloads.
next_probe: Use real-workload replay for product lag; use Chromium tracing only for benchmark-artifact mechanism.
